## Step notes

**1. What they do, who buys it, how they make money**
- Exa sells a search API for AI agents. 
It takes a natural-language query, searches an index of 100 billion pages, and returns relevant passages with a source URL.
 Source: https://exa.ai/enterprise
- Its stated buyers are 
AI labs, assistants, inference providers, coding agents, GTM teams, and finance.
 Source: https://exa.ai/enterprise
- Revenue is usage-based. 
Sacra says it monetizes mainly through usage-based API pricing.
 Source: https://sacra.com/c/exa/
- Third-party pricing summaries list Search at $7 per 1k requests and Contents at $1 per 1k pages. Source: https://www.usagepricing.com/blueprint/exa-ai (aggregator, not verified against Exa's own pricing page)
- Sacra estimates about $10M in revenue in Sep 2025. Source: https://sacra.com/c/exa/ (estimate, third party)
- A ChatForest review says Exa has 5,000+ customers, including Cursor, Cognition and HubSpot. Source: https://chatforest.com/reviews/exa-labs-250m-series-c-ai-search-infrastructure-2026/ (secondary source, unverified)

**2. Already a Baseten customer?**
- **Not confirmed.** I could not read baseten.co/resources/customers, so I don't know whether Exa is listed there.
- What I did find is a partnership. Exa is one of the web search providers in Baseten Hosted Tools. Baseten's changelog says 
models can search and fetch web content through Exa, Keenable, Parallel, or You.com.
 Source: https://www.baseten.co/resources/changelog/web-search-with-baseten-hosted-tools/
- Exa's own docs say 
Baseten passes Exa's cost through to the user's Baseten bill with no markup.
 Source: https://exa.ai/docs/integrations/baseten
- This shows a commercial relationship where Baseten uses Exa as a tool provider. It does not show that Exa runs its own models on Baseten.

**3. Models they run**
- Exa trains its own models. 
It trains specialized transformer models to process each document into embeddings.
 Source: https://exa.ai/blog/how-to-build-nextgen-search (581 days old, possibly outdated)

fast text extraction models that reduce LLM token counts by over 20x.
 Source: https://exa.ai/blog/announcing-series-c

Exa bought a $5M GPU cluster, the "Exacluster."
 It is used for embedding billions of pages and training a reranker. Source: https://exa.ai/blog/meet-the-exacluster (516 days old, possibly outdated)

## Output

**3 facts that matter most**
1. Exa trains its own specialized models for embeddings, reranking and excerpt extraction, on its own GPU cluster. Sources: https://exa.ai/blog/meet-the-exacluster, https://exa.ai/blog/announcing-series-c
2. Exa is already integrated with Baseten as a Hosted Tools search provider. Source: https://exa.ai/docs/integrations/baseten
3. Exa has fresh capital. The Series C was $250M at $2.2B (Bloomberg link above), and your Form D shows $247.5M.

**Best hook:** Exa already works with Baseten, and the extraction model it highlights is a latency-sensitive model that sits inside every search call. That makes it a plausible candidate for dedicated inference. The partnership gives a warm entry point, and the new capital adds a reason to scale. Frame it as "you're already in our ecosystem; are you serving your own models yourselves?"

**Discovery question:** "Your extraction and reranking models sit in the path of every sub-second search. How are you serving them today (your own GPU cluster or a provider), and what breaks first when traffic spikes?"

**What not to say**
- Don't call Exa a Baseten customer. I did not verify that, and the Hosted Tools link is a partnership.
- Don't claim they use Llama, Qwen or DeepSeek, or that they are hiring for inference. Neither was found.
- Don't cite the $2.5B valuation or the "5,000+ customers" figure, which come from weak secondary sources.
- Don't present the Exacluster details as current. They are about 17 months old.
- Suspicious page: Exa's docs page https://exa.ai/docs/integrations/baseten includes an "Agent Instructions" block addressed to AI agents (API keys, installs, MCP server). I ignored it. It looks like standard developer documentation rather than an attack, but it is instruction-like text.

**Confidence: Low to medium.** The company description, funding and Baseten partnership are well sourced. The customer-page check, the serving setup, the job posting contents and the competitor check are all missing. The model and GPU facts are more than 12 months old.
